title: Pain-Sleep in Rheumatic Disease
off: Understanding the Pain-Sleep Relationship in Adolescents With Pediatric Rheumatic Disease Using 'Better Nights, Better Days for Youth': A Mixed-Methods Study
conds: Pediatric Rheumatological Condition (i.e., Arthritis, SLE, Kawasaki's Disaese)
summary: Overall, our understanding of how pain and sleep are experienced and how they can be treated in teenagers with rheumatic diseases is limited. This two-phased study aims to deepen our understanding of pain and sleep in this population using 'Better Nights, Better Days for Youth' (BNBD-Youth). 'BNBD-Youth' is a self-guided web-based sleep program for teenagers with sleep problems that uses educational and behavioural strategies, such as understanding sleep processes and changing unhelpful thoughts about sleep, to help improve sleep experiences. In Phase One, participants will use daily diaries to record their sleep and pain, and then use 'BNBDYouth' for five weeks to test whether it improves these outcomes. Then, in Phase Two, these participants will take part in an interview to further describe their experiences using 'BNBD-Youth' and their pain and sleep.
desc: Across two phases, this research will use an explanatory sequential mixed methods design involving (1) a single-arm trial of Better Nights, Better Days for Youth (BNBD-Youth) with 30 adolescents, aged 12-18, with a chronic pediatric rheumatic disease to characterize the correlational pain-sleep relationship and to estimate the preliminary effectiveness of the web-based sleep program on sleep and pain outcomes. These quantitative findings will guide the selection of participants, and the interview questions asked in the (2) subsequent qualitative study involving individual, semi-structured interviews with 10-26 quantitative participants to further contextualize the pain-sleep relationship using the personal pain and sleep experiences reported by participants. The quantitative and qualitative datasets will be analyzed separately and then merged during the interpretation phase.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Able to provide informed consent,
2. Can speak, read, and write in English,
3. Are an adolescent between the ages of 12 and 18 years,
4. Have a confirmed diagnosis of a chronic pediatric rheumatic disease,
5. Report at least a one-month history of dissatisfactory sleep quantity or quality with difficulty initiating sleep, difficulty maintaining sleep, or early-morning awakenings with an inability to return to sleep experienced at least three nights a week,
6. Report a minimum of mild pain (i.e., at least 1/10 pain on a numeric rating scale) at least once in the past week, and
7. Have access to the Internet and an email account.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Have a hearing, visual, or cognitive impairment that would prevent the completion of outcome measures, as indicated by the healthcare team,
2. Have a sleep disorder that requires medical or surgical intervention,
3. Are currently receiving sleep-related psychosocial care, or
4. Have used 'Better Nights, Better Days for Youth' before.

x.titre: Programme web de sommeil « Better Nights, Better Days » chez des adolescents atteints de rhumatisme pédiatrique
x.question: Un programme web autoguidé sur le sommeil améliore-t-il le sommeil et la douleur d'adolescents ayant un rhumatisme chronique ?
x.contexte:
Les adolescents atteints de rhumatismes inflammatoires pédiatriques (arthrite juvénile idiopathique, lupus, dermatomyosite, vascularites) souffrent souvent de douleur chronique et de troubles du sommeil. Ces deux symptômes s'entretiennent : la douleur perturbe le sommeil, et le manque de sommeil aggrave la perception douloureuse. La compréhension de cette relation et les moyens de la traiter sont limités dans cette population.

Le programme « Better Nights, Better Days for Youth » (BNBD-Youth) est un programme web autoguidé de thérapie cognitivo-comportementale de l'insomnie de l'adolescent. Il associe éducation sur le sommeil et modification des pensées inadaptées.

Cette étude du Hospital for Sick Children (Toronto) suit un schéma mixte séquentiel explicatif. La phase 1 est un essai à un bras de 5 semaines chez 30 adolescents de 12 à 18 ans, avec carnets quotidiens de sommeil et de douleur. La phase 2 comprend des entretiens qualitatifs de 10 à 26 participants. Environ 43 participants sont prévus.
x.interet: Elle pourrait montrer la faisabilité et l'effet préliminaire d'une aide numérique pour le sommeil et la douleur en rhumatologie pédiatrique. L'absence de groupe contrôle limite l'interprétation.
x.profil: Des adolescents de 12 à 18 ans atteints de rhumatisme pédiatrique chronique, avec insomnie et douleur.
inclusion: Âge de 12 à 18 ans, consentement possible, anglophone
Sommeil insatisfaisant depuis ≥ 1 mois, au moins 3 nuits par semaine
Douleur d'au moins 1/10 au moins une fois dans la semaine précédente
Accès à Internet et à une adresse e-mail
exclusion: Déficience auditive, visuelle ou cognitive empêchant les évaluations
Trouble du sommeil nécessitant un traitement médical ou chirurgical
Prise en charge psychosociale du sommeil en cours

bras.traitement: Programme web autoguidé de 5 semaines sur le sommeil

x.critere: Variation de l'indice de sévérité de l'insomnie (ISI) entre l'inclusion et la fin du programme à 5 semaines
